consequence.statement: The etcd.managed Helm configuration value will no longer be honored in Cilium 1.16.0; environments using this setting must migrate to an alternative etcd deployment method.
consequence.remediation: Remove the etcd.managed configuration and any related etcd Helm values from your values.yaml. Deploy etcd independently or use an existing etcd cluster without relying on Cilium's managed etcd functionality.

original.statement: The Helm option for deploying a managed etcd instance via etcd.managed and other related Helm configurations have been removed.

consequence.statement: The etcd.managed Helm value and related managed-etcd Helm settings have been removed in 1.16.0. If an environment still sets them, they are no longer honoured. The upgrade notes do not say what replaces them.
consequence.remediation: Find any etcd.managed or related managed-etcd values in your Helm values and remove them before upgrading. Decide how etcd is provided without the removed Helm option.

corrected.statement: In Cilium 1.16.0 the Helm option etcd.managed (deploying a managed etcd instance) and related Helm settings were removed. If these values are still set, they are no longer honoured.

decision.reason: [ev-d6d613eadc25] says the `etcd.managed` Helm option and related Helm settings "have been removed". A removed Helm key that is still set stops being honoured, so setting-ignored is the right kind. The proposed statement and remediation go further than the evidence: they say operators "must migrate to an alternative etcd deployment method", tell them to deploy etcd independently, and set severity to high. The evidence says none of this, so I narrowed the statement to what the text supports.
